body:
The month

First of the month. You decided to actually write in this thing instead of just tapping keep.

The kettle took forever and you let it. The kettle was in the middle of a sentence, and nobody had told it how the sentence ended.

The light in the hall at eight is the colour of weak tea and you've walked through it every morning for two years without once looking at it.

I've bet the Index a biscuit about how this ends.
title: The month

body:
The end piece

The man at the bakery remembered you like the end piece.

You looked at the stairs for a long time. I counted.

The Quillquarium splashed a first-year from the far end this morning, uphill, and apologised in bubbles.

The Index wants to see my working for the biscuit bet. I haven't got any working. I've got a feeling.

Purest form

I've raised the biscuit bet to two biscuits. The Index is pretending not to be tempted.
title: Purest form

body:
The lamp

Long walk. You took the path by the water because the main road was loud, and there was a heron standing in the shallows so still that two kids were arguing about whether it was real. The heron stood in the shallows like it had been asked to wait and was determined to do it properly.

It moved its head about an inch and one of them screamed.

You laughed out loud on your own like an idiot and didn't care. Home by four. Rain by four-fifteen. Good timing for once.

I lost the bet. The Index ate the biscuit in front of me, slowly, with a book open. I'll remember that.
title: The lamp

body:
A people

Professor Permancer's bookmarks hang in a row by the Vault door. Each one lifts when its name is said in the corridor.

I have been meaning to write, which is a thing people say when they mean they have been avoiding the pen. The truth is simpler: you were in the corridor on Tuesday, looking at the stair as if it had said something, and I didn't ask what. I regret that.

I'm writing a rude letter to the rain, and I'm not going to send it.

The Kitchens

Tidied the shelf of things you never use at Amanda's.

The kettle in the Kitchens has opinions about you. Don't ask.

You kept thinking about it on the bus.

A castle keeps turning up in the margins of the common-room books, in a hand nobody knows.

I'm counting the stairs slowly, one at a time.

title: The Kitchens

body:
A new route

Tried a new route to work at the library. The library hummed with all the sentences it wasn't allowed to say aloud. It was cloudy, and the moon was a waning crescent.

The guild met in the Corridor of Whispered Secrets. Someone had left a note in a book from 1974: 'Look up.' You added one underneath.

You told Amanda about it later.

The Old Reading Room has been warmer than the rest of the building all week. People go in to get warm and come out thinking about something else.

My rude letter to the rain is three pages long. Page two is only the word honestly.

Low grey sky

Low grey sky sitting right on the roofs like a lid.

You like it more than you should.

It makes the street feel like a room.

I sent the rude letter. I know. Don't look at me. It went out of the window by itself.

The heavy shopping

Carried the heavy shopping up all four flights in the park by the war memorial.

I didn't leave the pen in your bag. Check the other bag.

Shirley said it was typical of you.

The lamps along the corridor to the East Stacks lean away from the door, like people stepping round a puddle.

The rain wrote back to my rude letter. It's one drop on the sill, and it's polite about it.

The toast

Burned the toast and ate it anyway before breakfast.

Rain on the bus window
the market closing its doors


Your brother would have loved it.

Swapped recipes with the woman from 3B after work.

You're writing it down so you remember.

Something knocks twice on the inside of the East Stacks door at the end of each afternoon, and waits politely to be answered.

I'm giving everything in the room an opinion.

body:
Next door

Walked the dog from next door at Amanda's. Small thing. Still counts. It was cloudy, and there was no moon.

Nothing happened today, which you're writing down because the Book keeps saying nothing is wasted. The book had a spine that remembered every place it had been bent.

So: you did the washing.

You ate toast standing up. You sat on the back step for ten minutes with your coat on and watched next door's cat try to get into the recycling. It failed. It tried again. Respect. You keep thinking about the stair that creaks only on the way down. You tested it tonight. It's true. You don't know why that pleases you so much, but it does.

Penny is writing the Bleed with the window shut for the first time this term. Her ink won't dry until someone reads it.

The chair thinks it's too early. The lamp thinks it's too late. The kettle has no opinion and it's smug about it.

The singing bird

Wrote a list and then lost it at the library. It was raining, and there was no moon.

Exercise: find something ordinary and make it answer. You chose a doorknob. It answered in a small cold voice.

It was nearly dark by then.

6 days ago: Tried a new route to work at the library.

Every clock near the East Stacks has stopped at a different time. Soren says they aren't broken, only undecided.

I asked the door what it thinks of me. It stayed shut. I'm taking that as respect.
title: The singing bird

body:
A brass plate

The library's back door has a brass plate worn silver in exactly the shape of a thumb.

A door by the north stair has begun to listen. It likes your footsteps.

3 days ago: Walked the dog from next door at Amanda's.

Professor Villanelle has started every lesson this week by asking the class to put their pens down and listen to the walls.

I've hidden one word somewhere in the building, and I'll know by morning if anyone found it.

The river

Found a coin with a hole through it by the river. The river had somewhere to be and said so quietly all day.

You should do that more often.

Somebody moved my hidden word. I know because it's the wrong way up.

body:
Your lunch break

Heard someone practising the trumpet on your lunch break.

It was colder than it looked.

Ironed a shirt for no reason on the way home. Nobody else noticed. Hard day.

You won't write all of it. You called your brother and you talked about nothing for forty minutes, which was the point. When you hung up the flat was very quiet and you put the radio on just to have someone else in the room. It was a programme about bees. You listened to the whole thing. 8 days ago: It makes the street feel like a room.

Wicker's been seen with a pencil behind each ear. Neither is his, and both are warm.

I've decided to be pleased about my hidden word being moved. It means somebody's reading the building.

A bus timetable

Helped a stranger read a bus timetable while the kettle boiled. You nearly missed it. The kettle had boiled for people for eleven years and had never once been asked what it thought. It was raining, and the moon was at its first quarter.

The man with the ladder had been a lighthouse keeper once, in another life, and still looked up at ceilings as if expecting ships.

Changed the bulb in the bathroom on the top deck of the bus.

You didn't take a photo, on purpose.

16 days ago: The kettle took forever and you let it.

The loaf on the Kitchen table has a row of small round holes along one side. Ambrose has counted them twice and won't say the number.

My hidden word came back with another word stuck to it. Now there are two. I don't know whose is whose.

The window box

Ate lunch on a bench facing the wrong way in the rain.

Your hands smelled of it all evening.

Planted garlic in the window box in the hallway. The box held the shape of what had been in it for a week after.

That was the best part of the day. Untangled a necklace for twenty minutes in the park by the war memorial. The light was doing something odd. The blue door, 7:52 a.m. 17 days ago: The light in the hall at eight is the colour of weak tea and you've walked through it every morning for two years without once looking at it.

I'm writing a dragon into the margin. A small one.

I have been meaning to write, which is a thing people say when they mean they have been avoiding the pen. The truth is simpler: you were in the corridor on Tuesday, looking at the lamp as if it had said something, and I didn't ask what. I regret that.

You kept thinking about it on the bus.

15 days ago: Rain by four-fifteen.

The door to the East Stacks has a notice on it in Professor Permancer's handwriting. It was longer yesterday.

The dragon has opinions about the margin. It says it's too narrow. It's right.

The car roof

Frost on the car roof in the shape of a map of somewhere that doesn't exist.

6 days ago: The library's back door has a brass plate worn silver in exactly the shape of a thumb.

The Kitchens smell of bay leaf and wet stone. Ambrose says that's the stone's fault.

I've given the dragon a bigger margin. It's asked for a window, a chair and a dry bit of bench.

The table

The East Stacks are shut. Serenity's awake in the Kitchens. I've kept a place for her map; it keeps moving when nobody touches it.

Your handwriting got braver this week. Don't tell anyone I said so.

The dragon's asleep on the page. I closed the book gently around it. It's snoring in the Index's ear. The Index is being brave.
title: The table

body:
A story

Bought flowers for no one in particular before breakfast.

It was nearly dark by then.

12 days ago: Burned the toast and ate it anyway before breakfast.

Tonight I'm counting everything with a lid. So far it's eleven, and one of them is a cat.
title: A story

body:
The bakery

Learned the name of the bakery cat after work.

The mirror said you looked like someone who had been listening to a long story and had just reached the good part.

It rained again right after.

You tried the thing from the Wayfinding class, mapping the street by smell, on the way home.

Bakery, then the laundrette (hot cotton), then the bins behind the chip shop, then nothing for a long stretch, then woodsmoke from somebody's chimney two roads over. You'd never have noticed the woodsmoke if you hadn't been playing. You stood at the corner for a while just breathing it in like a weirdo. You think that's what this whole Book is for, honestly. Making you stand on corners. 21 days ago: The man at the bakery remembered you like the end piece.

Rooms that belong in other books lean in at the windows to see how the Academy does things.

I'm practising being quiet. I'm bad at it.

The post box

Oiled the squeaky kitchen door late at night. The kitchen smelled of three different days at once and was fond of all of them.

The kettle had been working up to it for years. Tuesday, it said, in a small steam voice, and nothing else. So on Tuesday nothing was done about anything, and it was a very good day.

Shirley said it was typical of you.

Counted the steps to the post box at Amanda's. Nobody else noticed. The river, going gold.

15 days ago: Shirley said it was typical of you.

Somebody is playing a slow tune on a harpsichord in a room that isn't on the map. The Academy hums along and loses its place.

I'm teaching myself to whistle. I haven't got the lips for it and I'm doing it anyway.

The river

Wore odd socks all day at the library.

Where Things Are Now

If one column gets read this week, make it this one. The Academy has company. A composite castle has grown through the East Stacks, which remain shut.

Sat with Amanda while she waited for news by the river.

The radio was playing something old. Tidied the shelf of things you never use on your lunch break. You didn't take a photo, on purpose. 18 days ago: You told Amanda about it later.

There's a stair between the supper tables. I've caught a loose moon in my ribbon. We need to get these rooms home before the rest of the library follows them out.

Tonight I'm holding the pen steady.

That you missed writing in here on the two days you didn't.

I've caught a loose moon in my ribbon. It's heavier than it looks, and it hums.

A Quiet Night

I did a whole whistle. It was one note. It was a good note.

body:
A composite castle

Several Places, One Entrance

A composite castle has grown through the East Stacks overnight. It's built, in order, of a library, a fortress, and a nursery. The Quillquarium drawbridge is real and closed to visitors.

I'm timing how long it takes a candle to forget it's a candle.

body:
The back step

Wrote your brother a postcard on the back step.

The Count Returned

Dracula is back in *Dracula.* The borrowed rooms have gone home to their books, the stair is a stair in a story again, and the drawbridge has been returned to the Quillquarium's nibs with an apology and a quantity of ink. Serenity Brown still hears the crossings.

You don't know why it stayed with you.

Last real day of October.

You read back through the month on the bus and there's more in it than you thought. The heron. The stair. The bees. The woodsmoke. None of it's anything, and all of it's the month. You want to remember that it was a month where you started looking up. 19 days ago: You sat on the back step for ten minutes with your coat on and watched next door's cat try to get into the recycling.

It was clear, and the moon was a waning gibbous. The sky showed thin, high clouds moving fast. A single star blinked out once.

I'm giving everything in the room an opinion.

The record

There's a loose stitch in my spine. Penny says to stop poking it. I'm going to poke it later.

October, Corrected

The month, for the record. A Jump went wrong on a Sunday, the Count came out of his book, and the East Stacks shut. A composite castle, a drawbridge and a nursery window moved in.

The chair thinks it's too early. The lamp thinks it's too late. The kettle has no opinion and it's smug about it.
